items.title: BMJ Group, Sage and more to share 20m research papers with AI company Redpine
items.excerpt: Five academic publishers (BMJ Group, Sage, IOP Publishing, IGI Global and Wanfang Data) struck a deal giving Redpine's AI agents licensed access to 20 million peer-reviewed papers, a new licensing model for publisher content.
items.rationale: New concrete licensing deal: five publishers open 20m peer-reviewed papers to Redpine's AI agents, a fresh model for licensing publisher content to agents rather than for training.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Historian Jill Lepore Speaks of an Industry—and a World—'On the Knife Edge of History'
items.excerpt: At Frankfurt's opening press conference, where AI was called 'the issue on everyone's minds', Jill Lepore warned against handing the future to tech moguls, and German publishers' chair Sebastian Guggolz said AI cannot make up for falling reading competence.
items.rationale: Frankfurt 2026 opened yesterday with AI named the issue on everyone's minds; this is the fair's own opening press conference, not the 9/25 PW preview.

items.title: Kevin Roose Didn't Use AI to Write His Book About AI
items.excerpt: On WIRED's Big Interview, the author of The AGI Chronicles says his book 'was written by a very tired, overworked, under-slept human being', and talks about where AI fits, and doesn't, in writing a book.
items.rationale: A high-profile AI author on where AI does and doesn't belong in writing a book; timely given the disclosure scandals and an author's-eye view next to the industry picks.

items.title: Research Integrity in Scholarly Communications — SSP Pulse Check Report
items.excerpt: SSP's latest Pulse Check survey shows how scholarly publishers are dealing with research integrity as paper mills, manipulation and generative-AI-made submissions put integrity systems under strain.
items.rationale: New survey data on how scholarly publishers are handling integrity strain from generative-AI submissions and paper mills; the writer must lead on the AI findings.

items.title: LibreOffice says 'no AI' is now a software feature
items.excerpt: The open-source document editor used by many writers says it won't add AI to its default configuration, citing user privacy, and is pitching 'no AI' as a feature against Word and Docs.
items.rationale: A writing tool announces it will keep AI out of its default setup and markets that as a feature against Word and Docs; a direct choice for writers who want to avoid AI in their drafting software.
